knowledge.text: For the current Skill's microwave clause (when holding the target at a microwave, use the direct `heat <object> with microwave <n>` action before moving the object in, rather than moving it in and closing to heat it later), candidate adherence to the direct action coincided with success in cases where the parent cycled the door without ever heating. In 'heat some tomato and put it in countertop', parent P4 never issued a heat action and failed at the 50-step limit while toggling microwave 1 open/closed (P4:6, P4:40, P4:50), whereas candidate Q4 held tomato 2 at microwave 1 and used `heat tomato 2 with microwave 1` at Q4:5, then placed it on countertop 1 at Q4:7 and succeeded in 7 steps. In 'put a hot potato in fridge', candidate Q3 direct-heated the held potato at Q3:5 and finished in 12 steps, while parent P3 began by opening, filling, and closing microwave 1 without heating (P3:4-P3:6) and succeeded only later, in 20 steps, after taking potato 3 and direct-heating it at P3:17. The direct-heat clause is not sufficient and does not explain every paired difference: candidate Q1 also direct-heated while holding (Q1:7) but heated cup 2 instead of the mug the task required and never placed any object in coffeemachine, so both P1 and Q1 failed at the step limit; and in 'heat some plate and put it in cabinet' both P2 (P2:24) and Q2 (Q2:6) used direct heat, so that pair's 8-vs-27 step difference is not attributable to this clause.

In the initial Manipulation Skill edit, the hold-and-invoke state-change guidance matched behavior when the required object was acquired: in heat some egg and put it in countertop, parent P9 moved egg 1 into microwave 1 and repeatedly opened/closed it until the 50-step limit, while candidate Q9 took egg 1, opened microwave 1, used `heat egg 1 with microwave 1` while holding it, then placed it on countertop 1 and succeeded in 9 steps. Similarly, hot apple in fridge P8/Q8 both used hold-heat and succeeded (P8 14 steps, Q8 8 steps with no microwave opening), and cool bread in countertop P3/Q3 and P4/Q4 used hold-cool with fridge 1 before placing. Limit: this is a joint initial Skill, and in the cool tasks the parent also sometimes already used hold-cool, so the edit is not uniquely responsible; candidate Q10 later applied heat to the wrong cup and still failed.

Named-object selection was only partially effective. Candidates took the correct named object in several tasks (Q3/Q4 took bread 1 for cool bread, Q8 took apple 1 for hot apple, Q9 took egg 1 for heat egg), but Q7 for cool pot first took pan 1 from stoveburner 2 and moved it, took pot 2 only at Q7:49, and hit the step limit; Q10 for heat mug took cup 1 from cabinet 8 and heated the cup, also failing. In P5/Q5 (cool pan), parent took pot 1 despite the pan task and candidate never acquired the pan; both failed. Parent P7 likewise took pan 1 first but then recovered to pot 2 and succeeded in 20 steps. This shows the clause did not consistently prevent wrong-type acquisition, and wrong-type acquisition was associated with candidate failure in P7/Q7 and P10/Q10.

Search/recovery guidance had mixed outcomes. In cool bread in countertop P4/Q4, candidate Q4 found bread 1 on diningtable 1 and completed in 8 steps, while parent P4 succeeded only after 47 steps; Q3 also finished one step faster than P3. But candidate Q6 did not cover a plausible container: parent P6 opened cabinet 9, took plate 1, cooled it with fridge 1, and placed it on diningtable 1 in 43 steps, whereas candidate Q6 hit the 50-step limit and its recorded trajectory ended without taking a plate, cycling among countertops and cabinets 1-4. In P7/Q7, parent recovered from wrong pan 1 to correct pot 2 and succeeded in 20 steps, while candidate Q7 took pot 2 only at step 49 and failed at the limit; in P2/Q2 neither side found the bread and both hit the limit. Thus the guidance did not uniformly improve efficiency and did not guarantee coverage of all plausible containers.

Despite the action-format clause, candidate adherence to admissible commands was not uniform. Candidate Q6 still emitted inadmissible `go to cabinet 3` at Q6:6 and `go to cabinet 2` at Q6:16 when those were not in the current admissible list; Q6 ultimately failed. Other candidate runs (Q3, Q4, Q8, Q9) completed using admissible actions throughout, and candidate Q9 specifically avoided parent P9's malformed/door-toggling failure. Thus valid-action adherence appeared in some success cases but did not eliminate invalid commands in candidate runs.

Clean hold-transform-place guidance was preserved: in clean some spoon and put it in diningtable P1/Q1, both sides took spoon 1 from drawer 2, cleaned it at sinkbasin 1 while holding it, and moved it to diningtable 1; candidate Q1 succeeded in 10 steps versus parent P1 in 9 steps, with the extra candidate step being an initial countertop 1 check. This shows no regression in the clean sequence, though the search detour was not required.

For the current Skill's multi-instance clauses (return to a location that still shows a needed instance; place each carried instance in the same receptacle as an already-placed instance; do not relocate already-placed instances), candidate runs that consolidated both instances in one receptacle succeeded where the parent scattered or relocated them. In 'put two candle in drawer', parent P6 placed candle 1 in drawer 1 (P6:5) and candle 2 in drawer 6 (P6:21), and also moved an already-placed candle between drawers (P6:26, P6:42), failing at the 50-step limit; candidate Q6 took candle 1 and candle 2 from countertop 1 and placed both in drawer 3 (Q6:9, Q6:13), returning to countertop 1 for the still-visible second candle (Q6:10-Q6:11), and succeeded in 13 steps. Preserved consolidation also occurred in 'find two newspaper and put them in sofa' (both sides placed both newspapers in sofa; P8:4/P8:11 vs Q8:5/Q8:9; Q8 9 steps vs P8 11) and 'put two saltshaker in sidetable' (both placed both saltshakers in sidetable 1; P9:4/P9:10 vs Q9:4/Q9:11; Q9 11 steps vs P9 10, the candidate's extra step being a diningtable 1 detour).

Where a second required instance was not located, the current multi-instance/search guidance did not yield success, did not ensure coverage of unvisited plausible locations, and candidates still re-checked the same subset. In 'find two cd and put them in drawer' both P5 and Q5 failed at the 50-step limit; candidate Q5 cycled shelves and drawers (e.g., Q5:12-Q5:20, Q5:30) and never visited dresser 1, where parent P5 found and took a cd (P5:11-P5:12). In 'find two keychain and put them in armchair' both P7 and Q7 failed at the limit after each found only keychain 2 on sidetable 2 and placed it in armchair 1 (P7:36-P7:38; Q7:16-Q7:18); the candidate then repeatedly revisited drawers and sidetables without acquiring a second keychain. Because no second instance was acquired, whether one existed and its location are unknown.

For a relational task outside the edited clauses, no regression was observed, but the difference is not attributable to the edit because the diff contains no desklamp-related guidance: in 'look at alarmclock under the desklamp' both P10 and Q10 turned on desklamp 1 (P10:2; Q10:2) and then took alarmclock 2 (P10:5; Q10:3), succeeding in 5 and 3 steps respectively.
